points.description: Argues that at steady state all derivatives vanish, including the integrator state's derivative ξ̇ = r − θ, so ξ̇ = 0 forces θ = r exactly, independent of the values of b and c (a, b, c do not appear in the argument). Should note the closed loop must be stable so a steady state is reached. Merely restating that the error is zero, or computing it only for the specific values a=2, b=1, c=6, does not earn the mark.

levels.says: Says the integrator forces zero error at steady state but does not clearly link ξ̇ = r − θ = 0 to θ = r, or does not make clear it is independent of b and c.

points.description: Names one valid practical failure mode of integral action together with its matching standard remedy. Acceptable pairs: integrator windup with anti-windup (clamping/conditional integration/back-calculation); reduced stability margin/added phase lag with lower KI or placing the integral pole slower than dominant poles; integration of sensor bias/offset with calibration or leaky integrator. Both failure mode and remedy are needed.

levels.says: Names a valid failure mode but gives no remedy or a wrong/mismatched remedy.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a clear argument that ξ̇ = r − θ = 0 at steady state gives θ = r independent of b, c (given stability), plus one valid failure mode with its remedy. Half marks for each point if only partly given. A failure mode listed with no remedy earns at most half of P2.
